rationale: Attempt-00 (block_M=32, block_N=64, block_K=32, stages=3, swizzle=0) passed all checks with simulated 147.72us, 33.82MB DRAM, 5 blocks/SM, 18KB smem. Since M=32, block_M=128 can never divide M and block_M=64 with N/K tiling would pitch tiles too large; block_M=32 is the only valid axis that divides M=32 exactly, so it is pinned. To improve utilization for this 32x4096x4096 shape we broaden swizzle to [0,4,8,16] to test the serpentine panel-reuse hypothesis against the row-major baseline, and keep block_N in {64,128} and block_K in {32,64} to explore larger tiles that should amortize A-traffic and increase AI, while num_stages is restricted to {2,3} since stages=1 under-pipelines and stages=3 already worked. shared_memory_limit stays at the 32768 hard portability cap; footprint weight kept at 1 to keep configs small enough for 5+ blocks/SM. Traffic weight raised to 1.5 because B (16M elements) dominates DRAM reads at ~33.8MB observed — reuse from swizzle would mainly affect A, so we will inspect simulated_dram_mb and simulated_us after feedback: if swizzle>0 does not reduce simulated DRAM or latency, downweight traffic to ~0.5-1.0 and steer toward block_N=128 and stages=2. Launches weight lowered to 0.5 because ceil(M/32)=1 so launch count is governed by N tiles only and is less discriminating. All choices are subject to divisibility and the estimate max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*stages, 4*block_M*block_N) <= 32768. Scope note: simulator results are estimates, not hardware measurements; Metal numerically checks the exact source/TIR/config but does not execute the CUDA binary. This is a local hypothesis based on one observed point, not a global optimality claim.
